sections.h2: How many property tax bills does a Yonkers homeowner get?
sections.html:
Two a year. The City of Yonkers sends one in March for Westchester County tax and one in July for city and school tax. The city's tax page says the county bill is paid once, usually in April, and the city and school bill is split into three equal installments with three stubs at the bottom.

Yonkers is the largest city in Westchester County, with 212,603 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, and the Tax Office sits in City Hall at 40 South Broadway. The Assessment Department in the same building sets the values that the bills are built on. The city offers an online property tax portal where any parcel can be researched for free.

  • Tax Office, City Hall Room 108: payments, bill copies and payment history. The owner can call 914-377-6138, 914-377-6141 or 914-377-6146.
  • Assessment Department, City Hall, phone 914-377-6200: parcel updates, exemptions and assessment appeals.
  • Cashier's Office, first floor of City Hall, Room 108: in-person payments.

sections.h2: When are Yonkers property taxes due?
sections.html:
For the 2026 and 2027 city and school bill, installments fall on July 24, 2026, October 6, 2026 and January 6, 2027. The first date moves each year because it is set 30 days after the City Council adopts the budget, usually in June. The second is always October 6 and the third is always January 6, shifted off a weekend.

The county bill is adopted around March and falls due 30 days later, so the 2027 date will depend on when the county passes its budget. As of mid-November 2026, the third city installment is the next one on the calendar.

sections.h2: What happens if I pay a Yonkers tax installment late?
sections.html:
Interest starts immediately, because the Tax Office allows no grace period on an installment. The rate is 15 percent a year, simple interest, calculated daily from the confirmation date through the day of payment. The city says it cannot waive that interest for any reason.

The office decides whether a payment arrived on time by the postmark on the envelope. Local banks no longer accept Yonkers tax payments, so mail goes to City of Yonkers, 40 South Broadway, Room 108, Yonkers, NY 10701. Online payment by credit card or electronic check is also available, and the Yonkers site points owners to Yonkers.MunicipalTaxPayments.com to see outstanding taxes.

If you receive a delinquent notice for a bill you already paid, mail a copy of the front and back of the check and any receipt to the Tax Office at City Hall. Owners who get a delinquent tax letter are told to review the parcel in the online portal for details.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Yonkers assessment?
sections.html:
File a complaint with the Board of Assessment Review between November 1 and November 15. Yonkers uses a fall calendar rather than a May grievance day. The Assessment Department's calendar sets a July 1 valuation date, an October 15 taxable status date and a November 1 tentative roll.

  • November 1 to 15: grievance period for complaints to the Board.
  • December 15: deadline to send additional information or ask for a personal hearing.
  • Last Monday in January through the third Friday in February: personal hearings.
  • April 10 to May 10: window to file Small Claims Assessment Review or certiorari, open only to owners who already filed a protest with the Board.

The final roll is published on April 10. If this year's window has already closed when you read this, the next one opens November 1, 2027, and an owner who plans to sell can mention a pending protest to the buyer.

sections.h2: When must Yonkers exemption applications be filed?
sections.html:
By October 15 each year. That is the deadline for senior citizen, disability and veteran exemption filings and renewals, and it moves to the next business day when it lands on a weekend or holiday. The Assessment Department asks owners to apply by September 15 if they can.

The exemption stays on the roll only if it is renewed, so a seller who has had one for years should confirm the renewal is current. Ask the Assessment Department at 914-377-6200 what is on file for your parcel.

sections.h2: What do title companies need from the Yonkers Tax Office?
sections.html:
They can research a parcel online for free, or they can pay a $5 fee per property per year for the Tax Department to research it. Title and mortgage companies are encouraged to use the city's online property portal and the municipal tax payment site first. Without a processed fee the office gives no information by phone or email, and it asks for two to three weeks of lead time.

Make checks for that fee payable to the City of Yonkers at 40 South Broadway, Room 108. If you are the seller, order the payoff early. Owners can also ask the Tax Office for copies of prior or current bills and for a history of payments.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Yonkers homes?
sections.html:
Yonkers has 81,645 households with an average of 2.53 people. Only 46.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so renters hold a majority, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $501,600 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $1,784.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $3,028, compared with $1,356 for owners without one. The median household income is $83,549, and 13.8 percent of residents live in poverty. The city covers 18.01 square miles of land, so density reaches 11,749.9 people per square mile. Mean commute is 35.6 minutes.

The city rises from the Hudson River up seven hills, and its downtown is Getty Square. Wikipedia notes that it has been a city since 1872 and that it stayed outside New York City when the 1898 consolidation was voted on. Check recent sales on your own block, since a citywide median hides neighborhood differences.

sections.h2: What should I check before selling a Yonkers house with tax due?
sections.html:
Start with the online parcel record, then confirm the exact figure with the Tax Office. Because installments carry no grace period, the date matters.

  • List which of the July, October and January installments are paid, and whether the April county bill is paid.
  • Ask for the interest through the planned closing date at 15 percent a year.
  • Check the exemption renewal date on October 15.
  • Find out whether a Board of Assessment Review complaint or a small claims case is pending.

A cash buyer does not need the taxes cleared first. The title company pays the open balances out of your proceeds at closing, and the Yonkers Tax Office can supply the payoff.

faqs.q: When is the next Yonkers property tax installment due?
faqs.a: The third city and school installment is due Wednesday, January 6, 2027. The next county bill is usually adopted in March and due 30 days later, with the 2026 date having been April 14.

faqs.q: How much is the late interest on Yonkers property tax?
faqs.a: It is 15 percent a year, simple interest, calculated daily from the confirmation date. There is no grace period, and the city says the interest cannot be waived for any reason.

faqs.q: When can I file a Yonkers assessment complaint?
faqs.a: From November 1 to November 15 with the Board of Assessment Review. Supporting documents and personal hearing requests are due by December 15, and hearings begin on the last Monday in January.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Yonkers taxes in person?
faqs.a: At the Cashier's Office on the first floor of City Hall, 40 South Broadway, Room 108. You can also mail a check to the same address or pay online by credit card or electronic check.

faqs.q: How can a title company get Yonkers tax information?
faqs.a: Title companies can use the online property portal and the municipal tax payment site for free. A $5 fee per property per year applies if the Tax Department does the research, with two to three weeks of lead time.
